title: Half of people missed the gorilla

lines.text: Half the people in this experiment missed a gorilla walking right in front of them.
In 1999, psychologists Daniel Simons and Christopher Chabris showed people a short video.
Two teams passing basketballs. The task was simple. Count the passes.
Partway through, a person in a gorilla suit walks right through the scene.

visual.label: a person in a gorilla suit

lines.text: About half the viewers never noticed it.
When your brain focuses hard on one thing, it can quietly filter out almost everything else.
Which means right now, there could be a gorilla in your life you're not seeing.

sources.claim: Simons and Chabris (1999): viewers counting basketball passes; about 50% failed to notice a person in a gorilla suit
